newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Chaos at Belgian ports as French strike goes on.
newsitem.headline: Chaos at Belgian ports as French strike goes on.

text.p: Lorries forced to detour through Belgium by the French road hauliers' strike clogged the country's ports on Thursday, with massive queues developing and lengthy waiting times to board ferries bound for Britain.

At Ostend a spokesman for Stena-Sally Lines reported sailings to Ramsgate fully booked for freight, with drivers having to wait in line for up to 10 hours to get on board. The spokesman said they were being given free coffee and sandwiches.

At Zeebrugge a spokesman for the port gendarmerie said queues of more than 1,000 trucks that built up on Wednesday had if anything got longer, with drivers having to wait up to 20 hours to get aboard sailings to Dover.
A spokesman for the Belgian Transport Association said the French strike, now in its 11th day and with settlement talks having broken down, was costing Belgian haulage firms millions of francs.

"It is impossible to get to Spain by road at all, and getting to Italy you have to detour through Luxembourg, Germany and Switzerland which has a 28-tonne weight limit," he told Reuters earlier this week.
The strike is also begining to bite Belgian industry.

The De Standaard newspaper reported on Wednesday that the Belgian plant of French car maker Renault had been forced to shut its doors temporarily because supplies of parts for assembly were stranded in France.
